description: I had a hot, dark cup of coffee—just water and ground beans, nothing added. It tasted burnt, but it helped me function.
I ate a blueberry muffin. Sweet and cakey, with soft crumbs and the occasional burst of fruit. It wasn’t warm, but it worked.
I had a shrimp salad tucked into a croissant—cold shrimp, mayo, maybe some dill. The croissant flaked all over the table.
I downed an espresso shot. Just bitter, concentrated coffee. It hit hard, like it was supposed to.
I ate an Italian sausage—probably pork, heavy on garlic and fennel. Juicy, greasy, and more filling than I expected.
I made some boxed mac and cheese. The noodles were soft, the cheese sauce was salty and artificial. Still hit the spot.
I added processed cheese—melted into goo. Not much to say, but it glued the meal together.
I tossed in some frozen peas. Sweet and mushy, straight from the microwave. They didn’t add much, but they were green.
I had a vanilla pudding cup—sweet and smooth, like cafeteria dessert. Familiar in a dull kind of way.
Oatmeal with brown sugar—warm, thick, and familiar. I eat it without tasting it.
